tEn: DoorDash Co-Founders on Agentic Commerce and the Future of Food Delivery
tZh: DoorDash 联合创始人谈智能体商务与食品配送的未来
sEn: DoorDash co-founders discuss how AI-driven natural language ordering is reshaping food and grocery delivery, and the role of robotics and data in their agentic commerce vision.
sZh: DoorDash 联合创始人讨论 AI 驱动的自然语言订购如何重塑食品和杂货配送，以及机器人和数据在智能体商务愿景中的作用。

consensus.en: DoorDash has invested in autonomy since 2018 starting with experiments and partnerships, then built DOT from a customer-use-case perspective.
consensus.zh: DoorDash 自 2018 年起以实验和合作方式投入自主技术，之后从客户用例出发自研了 DOT 机器人。

consensus.en: Natural-language ordering already moves the business: half of restaurant searches try new merchants, grocery baskets are 40 percent larger.
consensus.zh: 自然语言下单已带来显著变化：餐厅搜索中一半是尝试新商家，杂货订单金额平均高出约 40%。

consensus.en: Physical-world commerce is messy and nuanced, so DoorDash's billions of deliveries and drop-off data provide an unmatched edge.
consensus.zh: 实体商业世界杂乱且微妙，DoorDash 数十亿次配送与交付点数据构成难以复制的优势。

consensus.en: The future is a multimodal fleet—Dashers, DOT, drones, and sidewalk robots—all coordinated through DoorDash's local-commerce platform.
consensus.zh: 未来是 Dasher、DOT、无人机和人行道机器人组成的多模式配送网络，统一由 DoorDash 本地商业平台协调。

consensus.en: Once autonomy works, the hardest scaling problems shift to operations, hardware, manufacturing, and measuring AI return on investment.
consensus.zh: 自主技术跑通后，最难的规模化问题转向运营、硬件、制造以及衡量 AI 投入产出比。

contrarian.en: DoorDash originally bet on voice as the natural interface, but found conversational text is what actually landed with users.
contrarian.zh: DoorDash 原本押注语音是自然交互界面，结果发现对话式文本才能真正吸引用户。

contrarian.en: The right delivery robot is neither a sidewalk bot nor a robo-taxi, but an autonomous motorcycle-like vehicle for three-to-five-mile runs.
contrarian.zh: 真正合适的配送机器人既不是人行道机器人，也不是 RoboTaxi，而是面向 3~5 英里配送的摩托车式自动驾驶车辆。

contrarian.en: Ten years from now DoorDash will likely have more human Dashers than today, because demand growth requires every delivery modality.
contrarian.zh: 十年后 DoorDash 的人类 Dasher 很可能比今天更多，因为需求增长需要动用每一种配送方式。

contrarian.en: In physical-world AI, a general model alone is not enough; starting from technology and then finding a problem is backwards.
contrarian.zh: 在物理世界 AI 中，单靠通用模型远远不够；先造技术再找问题，这条路是反的。

contrarian.en: Real enterprise data often defeats frontier models that ace scrubbed benchmarks, exposing distribution gaps hidden by cleaned test sets.
contrarian.zh: 真实企业数据往往让在清洗后基准上表现出色的前沿模型失灵，暴露被干净测试集掩盖的数据分布差距。

turns.en: Question of how you got here. There is an insufficient supply of researchers and people who know how to work on robotics or applied AI in the ecosystem for the recognition of all the different cool use cases you go after. A lot of people gravitate toward the general case, like we can solve it once. I assume you're competing for some of those people. How do you convince people to work at DoorDash on these problems?
turns.zh: 你怎么走到这一步的？目前生态里，真正懂机器人技术或应用型 AI 的研究者和人才供给不足，没法覆盖你们去做的各种酷炫用例。很多人会倾向于做通用方案，觉得我们可以一劳永逸地解决一次。我猜你们也在争抢这批人。那你是怎么说服大家来 DoorDash 做这些问题的？

turns.en: Yeah, my pitch is really simple. It's basically like, do you want to go work on prototypes and demos and be at a PhD lab or do you want to work on something where you can actually ship something in the real world? I think that's really been the culture we kind of set up, both at DoorDash Labs and all the AI efforts: we're not just here to do pure research. At the end of the day, we get to ship something where we have real impact. I think people in the autonomy world for the past 10 years were fed up working on something for 10 years and never actually getting to a point where they saw their products being used in the real world. For us, we've always been much more focused on taking a practical approach. It's not about going to work on a crazy moonshot idea; it's about getting something out that can be shipped in the real world and actually start learning how these technologies interact with the physical world and start iterating. Because again, these things aren't built in a vacuum. You have to put something out in the real world, make contact with the real world, and actually learn from that. I think we did that pretty early on at DoorDash. Actually, I don't think a lot of people know, we've been doing autonomous deliveries in Phoenix for over two years now. We publicly announced last year that we've been doing it for over two years, but in the beginning it was just learning. It's one thing to do a fancy demo or have something that works in a one-off environment. It's entirely different to turn this into an actual scaled fleet, a scaled service, a scaled business. The thing I always talk about is that building an autonomy business takes more than just autonomy. It's about how you actually scale something in the real world. As you scale fleets, all of a sudden you're running into all these edge cases that you just don't see when you have to do something seven days a week, ten hours a day at scale. Things start breaking. It could be something as simple as dirt covering one of your camera sensors. How robust is your autonomy stack to handle that? Like there are leaves on the ground, but it only covers part of the road. Because again, our bot drives on the road but tries to act like a bike, so it takes the right side of the road or the bike lane. If there are leaves along where the sidewalks are, maybe half your wheels — the right two wheels are on the leaves, the left two wheels are still on the asphalt.
turns.zh: 我的说法其实很简单：你是想去做原型和演示，待在博士实验室里，还是想去做一些能在真实世界里真正落地的产品？我觉得这正是我们建立起来的文化，无论是在 DoorDash Labs 还是所有 AI 项目上——我们不只是来做纯研究的，最终我们要交付有真实影响力的东西。过去 10 年在自动驾驶领域，很多人已经厌倦了那些做了 10 年却从没看到产品真正在真实世界里被使用的工作。对我们来说，我们一直更注重采用务实、可落地的路径。不是去搞什么疯狂的登月计划，而是先把东西做出来、能在真实世界里交付，然后开始学习这些技术如何与物理世界互动，并不断迭代。因为再说一遍，这些东西不是在真空中造出来的。你必须把东西放到真实世界里，跟现实世界接触，并从中学习。我们在 DoorDash 很早就这么做了。说实话，没多少人知道——我们在凤凰城已经做了两年多的自动驾驶配送。我们去年才公开说这件事，但一开始真的只是在学习。就像你之前提到的，做一个炫酷的演示、或者在一次性环境中跑通某个东西是一回事；要把它变成一个真正的规模化车队、一项规模化的服务、一门规模化的生意，就完全是另一回事。我经常讲的一件事是：做自动驾驶生意，需要的远不止自动驾驶本身。你得思考如何在真实世界里规模化。当你要每周 7 天、每天 10 小时高强度规模化运营时，各种边缘情况就全跑出来了，这些在演示环境中根本看不见。事情开始出问题——可能是很简单的，比如有块泥巴遮住了摄像头传感器。你的自动驾驶技术栈能不能应对？比如地上有一些树叶，但它们只覆盖了部分路面。因为我们的小车是在马路上行驶，但会像自行车一样贴右边走，所以会走右侧车道或自行车道。如果沿着人行道边缘有落叶，可能一半轮子——右边两个轮子在树叶上，左边两个轮子还在柏油路上。

turns.en: Well, all of a sudden the torque you have to send to the wheels is very different, and your autonomy stack, your middleware, and your low-level controls have to handle that differently. That's something I would have never thought of if it was just driving in a nice little demo environment. Things just start breaking. How do you handle operations? People don't think about the non-autonomy operations required to scale autonomy. You have to set up depots. It's a physical world business. You have to set up depot maintenance. What about your battery? How do you recharge your battery? What if one of your braking systems over... here was an issue we ran into: there are certain situations where the vehicle has to brake so hard that the regenerative braking system overpowers the battery because it causes an electric shock. This only happens in extreme edge cases, but there are situations where you have to do that because something in the real world — safety is super important. So if it can't handle that, you got to figure it out. Another example we didn't think about is booting up the robots. When this was still a demo project, no one thought about boot up time. The original version of the robot boot up was a simple Jenkins script that one of our engineers hacked together in a couple hours, and it worked fine. But now you're doing hundreds of robots a day; every morning needs to get booted up, and the script crashes half the time. It takes 30-45 minutes, but multiply across 500 robots, all of a sudden it's like, holy crap, there's this huge productivity issue. And then, of course, you have to think through reliability. Now you have to start thinking about manufacturing supply chain, and of course the operational aspect: how does this thing interface with merchants? How do you handle the pickup drop-off problem? How do you educate the merchant? How do you even find the location of a customer's home? Which again sounds kind of silly, but when you punch in someone's address on Google Maps, the GPS pin — especially if you're going to an apartment complex — is never at the exact same spot. If you're a human, you kind of figure it out; you don't think about it. A human dasher shows up and can find where the restaurant is: this is the building, this is the front door. You can't do that with a robot.
turns.zh: 于是你发给车轮的扭矩就会非常不一样，你的自动驾驶技术栈、中间件和底层控制都得用不同的方式来处理。如果只是在漂亮的演示环境里开车，我永远不会想到这个问题。很多问题就是这样冒出来的。那你怎么处理运营？人们不会想到，要规模化自动驾驶，其实需要很多非自动驾驶的运营工作。你得建站点。这是门现实世界的生意，要有站点维护。电池怎么办？怎么充电？如果刹车系统……我们遇到过一个问题：在某些情况下，车辆必须紧急刹车，再生制动系统会反过来让电池过载，因为会产生电击。这种事只会在极端边缘情况下出现，但确实有必须那样做的场景，因为真实世界里安全极其重要。如果系统处理不了，你就得想办法。另一个我们没想到的问题是机器人开机。当这事还只是演示项目时，没人想过开机时间。最初机器人的开机方式，是我们一个工程师花几小时拼出来的一个简单 Jenkins 脚本，当时跑得挺好。但现在你每天要开几百台机器人，每天早上都需要启动，脚本一半时间会崩溃。它要花 30 到 45 分钟，但如果乘以 500 台机器人，突然就成了一个巨大的生产力问题。然后，当然，你还要考虑可靠性。你开始要思考制造和供应链，当然还有运营层面：这个东西怎么跟商家对接？取货和交付的问题怎么解决？怎么培训商家？甚至怎么找到顾客家的位置？这听起来有点蠢，但当你在地图里输入一个地址时，那个 GPS 定位点——尤其是去公寓楼的时候——从来都不是完全精确的同一个点。如果是人，你会自然而然找到，你不会多想。人类外卖员到了，能大概找到餐厅在哪：这是这栋楼、这是前门。但机器人做不到。

transcript.sec: Autonomy and vehicle scaling with Also

turns.en: Manufacturing, like, it's like learning all that, and that turns out to be a pretty hard problem at scale. So one of the things we actually did was partner up with this company called Also, which is a micromobility company that's spun out of Rivian. RJ is actually the board founder and chairman of the company. So we thought, why don't we work with someone who knows how to actually scale vehicles? So that's kind of one of the partnerships we struck up.
turns.zh: 制造，就像，学习这一切，结果发现这是一个相当难的规模化问题。所以我们实际做的一件事，是跟一家叫 Also 的公司合作，这是一家从 Rivian 拆分出来的微出行公司。RJ 实际上是这家公司的董事会创始人和董事长。所以我们想，为什么不跟一个真正知道如何规模化车辆的人合作呢？这就是我们达成的其中一项合作。

turns.en: But it's kind of funny. Like, the problem 5 years ago was autonomy. Now it's increasingly becoming more about operations, commercialization, hardware, manufacturing. And again, this is where DoorDash gets to shine with our scale advantage and operation advantage. How do we take this thing from not just 0 to 1, but like 100 to 1,000?
turns.zh: 但有点意思。5 年前的问题是自动驾驶，现在越来越变成运营、商业化、硬件、制造。而且，这正是 DoorDash 能发挥我们的规模优势和运营优势的地方：我们怎么把这个东西从 0 到 1，甚至是从 100 到 1,000？

turns.en: Yeah. One to three billion. Right. And I feel like DoorDash is just so well positioned to take this on. Like, we have just such a unique advantage here, and I think that's where we want to play in terms of playing to our strengths.
turns.zh: 对，10 亿到 30 亿。没错。而且我觉得 DoorDash 处于非常好的位置来做这件事。我们就是有这样的独特优势，而且我觉得这正是我们想发力的地方，发挥我们的优势。

transcript.secZh: 与Also的自主与车辆规模化

turns.en: So you have these enormous strengths. You've got the network and the existing great business, and these like two, you know, amongst others, I'm sure, like two really big plays around agent commerce and around autonomy. How do you think about—it's a 10,000 plus person company, and a lot of that company is ops, a lot of that company is technology. Um, and I'm sure you're thinking deeply about productivity of that workforce. Like, who owns it, what matters today, you're publishing benchmarks—talk about that.
turns.zh: 你有很多巨大的优势。你有网络、现有的大业务，还有这两个（当然我不确定还有别的）——智能体电商和自动驾驶这两大押注。你怎么看这家一万多人的公司？公司里很多是运营，很多是技术。我相信你肯定在深入思考这支劳动力的生产力，比如谁负责、现在什么最重要、你在发布基准测试——讲讲这个吧。

turns.en: I feel like in the past couple of years, what was required to really operate at a high level in the technology industry has changed a lot. And I think one of the reasons why we were so excited to acquire a company called Metis last year was really to just infuse some of that AI-native thinking into the company. I think for a company of our size, it's been... and I think every company—every large company at least—is facing this. I think a lot of startups, I mean you see this better than anyone else probably, the way they operate is so different. And I think a lot of people at our company have struggled to see what's possible because they're so used to how things have worked historically. So I think really figuring out how do we bring in people who have actually seen what is possible on the frontier, and incorporating that into how we do our work. And you know, coding is obviously the most obvious place to do transformation, and we've seen a lot of gains there. But there's also work we're doing in terms of how do we do AI enablement across the entire organization. So I think, figuring out how to benchmark various parts of the company. We announced a benchmark called Dashbench a couple of weeks ago, mainly focused on our ability to figure out how well various models and harnesses performed on coding tasks. And so that was a really good initial exercise for us to figure out how do we calculate the ROI on all this money we're spending. I mean, I was looking at it a week ago. Our spend in June went up like 20x versus what the spend was in January.
turns.zh: 我觉得过去几年，想在科技行业真正高水平运营，所需要的东西已经变了很多。所以我们去年收购一家叫 Metis 的公司时特别兴奋，就是想把一些 AI 原生思维注入公司。对我们这种规模的公司来说，这真的很……我觉得每一家公司，至少每家大公司，都面临着这个。很多创业公司——你大概比谁都看得清楚——它们的运作方式太不一样了。我觉得我们公司很多人因为太习惯于过去的工作方式，所以很难看到可能性。所以我想，关键是想办法把那些真正见过前沿可能的人引进来，并把它融入我们的工作方式。当然，编程显然是最明显的转型点，我们在那里看到了很多收益。但我们也做了些工作，关于如何在整个组织里做 AI 赋能。所以，我们在想如何给公司各个部分做基准测试。几周前我们发布了一个叫 Dashbench 的基准测试，主要关注我们在编程任务上评估各种模型和框架表现的能力。这对我们来说是一个特别好的初步练习，帮我们弄清楚怎么计算我们花掉的这些钱的 ROI。一周前我还在看这个数据，我们 6 月的支出比 1 月增长了大概 20 倍。

turns.en: Can I ask you—can you, uh, you don't have to answer—but since you've inspected this spend, has it come down, has it been flat, has it continued to grow?
turns.zh: 我能问一下——你其实可以不回答——但既然你看过这笔支出，它是下降了、持稳了，还是继续在涨？
嗯，我们在看到它趋于平稳。

turns.en: And whenever the shelf was getting empty, they would fire off the agent to basically restock the shelf. So I think those types of use cases that you wouldn't really think of—but I think it's going to unlock some interesting use cases that wouldn't really be as feasible or possible in today's world. But as we make things more naturally agent-first, I think some of these use cases are going to become a lot more interesting.
turns.zh: 每当货架快要空了，他们就会启动智能体去补货。所以我觉得，那些你可能不会想到的使用场景——我认为这会解锁一些在当今世界不太可行或不太可能的有趣用例。而随着我们让事物更自然地以智能体为优先，其中一些用例会变得更加有趣。

turns.en: Amazing. I love how ambitious you guys are for both the user experience and the scope and scale of DoorDash. Thanks, guys.
turns.zh: 太棒了。我特别欣赏你们在用户体验以及 DoorDash 的规模和范围上的雄心壮志。谢谢你们。

turns.en: Yeah, it's a pleasure to be here.
